events.title: ECMAScript 1 standard adopted (ECMA-262)
events.summary: Ecma adopted ECMA-262 1st edition in June 1997 — the first official standard for JavaScript and JScript.
events.about: ECMAScript is the vendor-neutral name for the language inside every browser. ECMA-262 gave Netscape JavaScript and Microsoft JScript a shared specification so web pages could rely on the same syntax across browsers. Every `document.querySelector`, promise, and module trace back to this standardization effort.

narrative.whyChosen: Standardization turned a browser arms race into a written contract developers could target.
narrative.whyImportant: It let JavaScript survive beyond Netscape and become the open web's programming language.
narrative.problemSolved: Without a standard, each browser vendor could fork the language and break the open web.

sources.title: ECMA-262 1st edition — adopted by Ecma General Assembly June 1997
